ao_demand_evidence.input: Calculate the actual length of a 21 mm specimen image shown at ×300 magnification. Give the answer in μm.
Cell A has an image 12 mm long at ×200 and cell B has an image 15 mm long at ×500. Calculate the actual length of each cell and say which cell is larger.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A is 12 ÷ 200 = 0.06 mm = 60 μm and B is 15 ÷ 500 = 0.03 mm = 30 μm. A is the larger cell, even though its image is shorter.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest why an unfamiliar root cell with a visible cellulose wall but no chloroplasts can still be classified as a plant cell.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The wall is plant-cell evidence; roots are not normally exposed to light and need not contain chloroplasts, so absence of chloroplasts does not outweigh the wall.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Fig. VIS-6116-3.2-03 is a photomicrograph of plant cells from a temporary slide. Draw the cells you can see as a labelled line drawing.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A correct drawing uses single, clear, unbroken outlines with no shading and shows the cells in their observed shapes and proportions. At least two visible structures, such as the cell wall, cytoplasm or nucleus, are correctly labelled. Each label line is drawn with a ruler and touches the structure named.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Fig. VIS-6116-3.2-04 is a photomicrograph of an animal tissue. Draw the cells as a labelled line drawing, showing how they are arranged and the nuclei that you can see.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A correct drawing uses single, clear, unbroken outlines with no shading. It shows the cells packed in the arrangement seen in the photomicrograph, with a nucleus drawn in each cell where one is visible. Visible structures such as a nucleus or the cell membrane are labelled with ruled lines.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Two cells of equal size receive the same oxygen supply. X must actively transport a much larger ion load per minute than Y. Suggest which is likely to contain more mitochondria and explain the link.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: X is likely to contain more mitochondria because its greater active-transport workload needs a higher rate of energy release through respiration.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Exchange unit X has twice the total surface area of Y, but an impermeable coat covers three-quarters of X. Y is fully exposed and other conditions match. Describe how the total diffusion rates compare.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: X has only half Y’s effective exposed area, because twice the area with a quarter exposed is half, so its total diffusion rate is expected to be lower.

ao_demand_evidence.input: A solute spreads faster in a cool shaken container than in a warm still container. A learner says this shows temperature does not affect diffusion. Describe why this conclusion is not justified.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The comparison does not isolate temperature because shaking adds bulk mixing. Faster spread in the cool container therefore does not disprove the effect of temperature on diffusion.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Two matched membrane systems are compared. In A the concentrations are 8 and 2 units on opposite sides; in B they are 8 and 6 units. Describe which should have faster net diffusion.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: A has the steeper difference, 6 units compared with 2 units for B, so faster net diffusion is expected if permeability and other conditions match.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Fluid collects between an oxygen source and some cells, so the total diffusion path increases from 4 μm to 12 μm. Other factors match. Describe the likely change in the rate of oxygen diffusion.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Exchange is expected to slow because the total path is now three times longer.

ao_demand_evidence.input: In the litmus demonstration the times to turn blue are 10 s, 25 s and 46 s at increasing distances. Suggest why these times do not by themselves show that particles move at a constant speed along the tube.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The litmus response is an arrival endpoint and diffusion is random motion, not a directed stream at one speed. The time differences, 15 s then 21 s, are not equal, so they do not support a constant-speed model.

ao_demand_evidence.input: In an investigation the time for a dye to reach a fixed point falls as temperature rises, and the volume of water and the colour endpoint are the same in every trial. Suggest what this shows.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The shorter times show faster diffusion to the same endpoint, consistent with greater particle kinetic energy at higher temperature, provided other relevant conditions were controlled.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Two enzyme chains contain the same number of amino acids, but the amino acids are in a different order. Explain why they could act on different substrates.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: Different order can cause different folding and active-site shapes. The substrates that fit those sites can therefore differ despite equal chain length.

ao_demand_evidence.input: An extract made with four times as much tissue gives a stronger sugar-test response. Suggest why this does not show that its region has more sugar per gram.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The stronger response may result from the greater tissue mass rather than a higher sugar content per gram. Standardise mass and extraction volume before comparing.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Enzyme X acts on substrate P but not on substrate Q, which is a similar size but has a different shape where it would bind. Explain why.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: P can interact correctly with X’s active site, whereas Q’s binding region does not fit/interact suitably. Similar overall size alone does not establish substrate compatibility.

ao_demand_evidence.input: One sample of an enzyme was chilled and another was heated enough to denature it. Both are then returned to 25 °C. Explain the likely difference between the two samples.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The chilled sample can regain activity as particles move faster again. The denatured sample is expected to remain less active because its active-site shape was altered, not simply slowed.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Two enzymes are tested at pH 2. One has an optimum near pH 2 and the other has an optimum near pH 7. Explain why they need not have equal activity.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The first is near its suitable optimum; the second is far from its optimum and may have impaired binding or denaturation. Different enzymes have different pH requirements.

ao_demand_evidence.input: Suggest why a lipase trial starting at a lower pH can reach an indicator’s colour endpoint sooner even if it does not produce fatty acid faster.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: It may need a smaller further pH change to reach that endpoint. Endpoint times from different starting pH values therefore do not necessarily measure comparable acid-production rates.

ao_demand_evidence.input: A biological powder removes a protein stain. Suggest why this does not show that the same enzyme removes an oily stain equally well.
ao_demand_evidence.inference_or_processing: The enzyme may be a protease with specificity for protein substrates. Oil is a different material and may need a lipase or other cleaning action.
